items.title: The counterfactual is estimated, not observed
items.whyItMatters: Every budget figure depends on what late users would otherwise have done, and the only estimates come from pharmacists and experts (claim c2).
items.opportunity: Extract counterfactual assumptions from every study and show budget impact across their range rather than a single figure.

items.title: Budget figures come from incompatible systems
items.whyItMatters: Perspective, price year, currency and offsets differ, so a pooled figure would mean nothing for this authority (claim c3).
items.opportunity: Re-express each estimate in 2026 prices and the authority's perspective in a structured table.

items.title: Staffing costs above the supplement are missing
items.whyItMatters: Owners paid for locums beyond the supplement and some cut hours (claim c5), so costings that omit this overstate value and sustainability.
items.opportunity: Extract staffing costs and service continuity wherever reported and flag their absence.

items.title: Who benefits from late opening
items.whyItMatters: A fifth of late users have no registered GP and people without a car need late bus routes, so location decides who is reached.
items.opportunity: Extract user characteristics and access by transport in both strands.

items.title: Displacement of demand
items.whyItMatters: Commissioners suspect demand moves from daytime services instead of falling.
items.opportunity: Treat displacement as a balancing outcome in the review.

errorsFound: The scheme's business case counts pharmacist-estimated avoided contacts as observed savings.
reevaluation: The gaps favour a review that shows budget figures across counterfactual assumptions in common prices and treats staffing, access and displacement as outcomes in their own right.
summary: Five gaps; the counterfactual and incompatible budget figures are high severity.
